clue.text: Joint, as in lock-up, primarily?

indicators.note: primarily asks for the leading letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether a joint is really the same thing as a lock-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: 'Joint' is slang for a prison, and the opening letters of the four words spell one.
explanation.definitionFit: Joint is underworld slang for a prison, a lock-up where offenders are held.

clue.text: After trial location, simple overlooking a polite act

indicators.note: after says the simple-word piece follows the trial-location piece

parts.note: a court is where a trial takes place

indicators.note: overlooking means leaving out, so the letter a is dropped from the word for simple

parts.note: simple means easy

explanation.surface: Instructions for courtroom etiquette: once in court, keep things simple and don't miss a polite gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking a' removes A from EASY, leaving ESY.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesy is a gracious, well-mannered gesture shown to someone.

clue.text: Large vehicle is hot — scarper!

parts.note: a van is a large road vehicle
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A getaway: the big van is too hot, so run for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scarper' is British slang for running away.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarper is to disappear quickly, making oneself scarce.

clue.text: Very smooth website's back-end covered in broken links

indicators.note: covered in means the website's final letter sits wrapped inside the rearranged letters
broken means the letters of links are smashed and reassembled
back-end asks for the final letter of the word website

explanation.surface: A web developer complains that a slick site's back-end is riddled with broken links.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges LINKS to SILKN, and 'covered in' puts E, the last letter of 'website', inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Silken describes something as soft and sleek as silk, hence very smooth.

clue.text: Distinct part of second feature in Glastonbury?

parts.note: Glastonbury Tor is the famous hill rising above the town; a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A query about which section of the Glastonbury music festival a second feature occupies.
explanation.walkthrough: Glastonbury is a town in Somerset, England, famous for its festival and for Glastonbury Tor, a hill; the question mark signals the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is a distinct area or division of a larger whole.

clue.text: Don't work some bread

definitions.meaning: a single baked block of bread

explanation.surface: A lazy baker's motto: skip work and have some bread.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to laze around; as a noun it is a shaped mass of baked bread.

clue.text: Oxen tire, desperately making effort

indicators.note: desperately suggests frantic disorder, so the letters of oxen tire are thrown around

explanation.surface: Ploughing oxen tire as they strain to keep pulling.
explanation.definitionFit: Exertion is physical or mental effort, the expending of energy.

clue.text: Deliberately wreck platform protecting characters inside Gabon

indicators.note: protecting means the platform word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a stage is a raised platform

indicators.note: characters inside asks for the middle letters of the word Gabon

explanation.surface: Saboteurs plan to wreck a platform shielding people inside Gabon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gabon' looks like part of the scene's geography, but only its central letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabotage is the deliberate damaging or obstruction of something, typically a plan or equipment.

clue.text: Church to copy front of Lord's religious building

parts.note: to ape is to imitate

indicators.note: front of asks for the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A church aims to copy the facade of a building at Lord's, the London cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous cricket ground in London; here only its first letter, L, is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small place of Christian worship, a type of religious building.

clue.text: I want the best for others, nearly everyone I kept in confidence

definitions.text: I want the best for others

indicators.note: nearly means the word for everyone loses its final letter

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: kept in means the letter I is held inside the word for confidence

parts.note: trust means confidence or faith

explanation.surface: A selfless person confides that they want the best for almost everyone they keep secrets for.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description in the first person of what such a person says.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone selfless, who puts the welfare of others first, would say they want the best for others.

clue.text: Peak of mountain's first crossed by expert

indicators.note: crossed by means the expert word spans the letter, which sits inside it

parts.note: an ace is an expert

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of mountain

explanation.surface: A mountain's summit being traversed by a skilled climber.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point, the summit of achievement or of a hill.

clue.text: Part of train caught, wedding top is taken off

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: top is taken off means the first letter of the wedding word is removed

parts.note: a marriage is a wedding

explanation.surface: A wedding party catches a train, and the top tier of the cake comes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top is taken off' removes M from MARRIAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A carriage is a passenger coach forming one section of a railway train.

clue.text: Rigid vessel suffering

parts.note: hard means rigid or firm
a ship is a sea vessel

explanation.surface: A stiff-hulled ship in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardship is severe suffering or privation.

clue.text: Chop times in A&E

indicators.note: in means the times letter goes inside the A&E letters

parts.note: A&E, accident and emergency, supplies the letters A and E
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: Chopping injuries at times land people in the hospital emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital's emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe something is to chop it, literally or in the sense of cutting it back.

clue.text: Y equals R, adjusted in a direct way

indicators.note: adjusted means the letters of Y equals R are reset into a new order

explanation.surface: An algebra problem in which one variable is set equal to another after adjustment.
explanation.definitionFit: Squarely means directly and without evasion, as in facing a problem head-on.

clue.text: Sign of ageing at temples, say, where things aren't black and white

definitions.text: Sign of ageing at temples, say
definitions.meaning: a patch of silvering hair, such as at the sides of the head

definitions.text: where things aren't black and white
definitions.meaning: a situation that is ambiguous, not clear-cut

explanation.surface: Greying temples as a mark of getting older, in a world no longer black and white.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a patch turned grey, such as hair at the temples; idiomatically an ambiguous zone between clear right and wrong.

clue.text: Tricky question of passenger's journey round start of District Line

indicators.note: round means the journey word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a ride is a journey taken as a passenger

indicators.note: start of asks for the opening letter of District

explanation.surface: A London Underground conundrum about a passenger's trip on the District Line.
explanation.walkthrough: The District Line is a London Underground line.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a puzzling question posed as a brain-teaser.

clue.text: Agreement, an uphill struggle in talks?

indicators.note: in talks means the word is as heard when spoken, so a word sounding the same is wanted

parts.note: an ascent is a climb, an uphill struggle

explanation.surface: Negotiators find reaching agreement in talks a hard climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is agreement or approval given to a proposal.

clue.text: Bone fragment in dreadful naan

indicators.note: fragment in means a short piece of the letters of dreadful naan is taken

explanation.surface: Finding a bit of bone in a terrible naan bread.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two long bones of the forearm.

clue.text: Enthusiast carrying weight is to be obsequious

indicators.note: carrying means the enthusiast word holds the weight letter inside it

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast

explanation.surface: A devoted fan lugging heavy gear for their idol is being servile.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn is to flatter or behave in a servile, grovelling way.

clue.text: Express contempt for Greek island in separate parts

parts.note: to dis someone is to show them disrespect
Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: Sneering at a Greek island that is divided into separate regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means individually distinct, made of separate unconnected parts.

clue.text: Band on the road, turning up regularly in Peer Gynt

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the selected letters are read from the bottom upwards
regularly asks for every other letter of Peer Gynt

explanation.surface: A road trip by a band playing music from Grieg's Peer Gynt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes ERYT from Peer Gynt, and 'turning up' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre is the rubber ring fitted around a wheel, the band that meets the road.

clue.text: Endless fogginess, a road danger

indicators.note: endless means the fogginess word loses its final letter

parts.note: haze is mist or fogginess

explanation.surface: Continuous fog is a menace to drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A hazard is a source of danger or risk.

clue.text: Publican left along with peer

parts.note: and means along with
a lord is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A pub owner leaves in the company of an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A publican, who runs a pub, is traditionally called the landlord in Britain.

clue.text: Change of name that is for an ungenerous person

indicators.note: change of means the letters of name are rearranged

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A stingy person changes their name to avoid paying up.
explanation.definitionFit: A meanie is a colloquial term for a stingy or unkind person.
